content.title: About
content.content: Rice, white, puffed (5901) is a processed rice that has been puffed to create light, crunchy flakes. It is commonly used as a snack, a dessert topping, and in Asian cuisine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Puffed rice originated in Japan in the early 20th century and quickly spread throughout Asian cooking.
Rice flakes contain almost no fat and are lower in calories compared with many other crackers.
Puffed rice is often used in baby foods because it is easy to digest and rarely allergenic.
The production uses whole rice grains without added flavors or colorants.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Puffed rice contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides slowly digestible carbs that help maintain steady energy levels.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: The puffing process retains some fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Rice is naturally gluten‑free, safe for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Provides B‑vitamins
items.content: Small amounts of B1, B3, and B6 are present, contributing to normal metabolism.

items.title: Rice allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to rice.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Puffed rice has a high GI, so people with diabetes should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Added salt
items.content: Some versions are salted; those limiting sodium should check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Puffed rice can be enjoyed as a snack, added to muesli, yogurt, ice cream, used as a dessert topping, sprinkled over soups, or incorporated into Asian dishes such as sushi rolls and rice balls.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from moisture and direct sunlight. Properly stored, it remains crunchy for up to 12 months.
